explicit_propositions.text: Representative Mike Rogers served 14 years in Congress and chaired the House Intelligence Committee from 2011 to 2015.
Rogers was an FBI agent and later became a national security commentator on CNN.
He hosted a TV series called 'Declassified, The Untold Stories of American Spies' on CNN.
Rogers was commissioned an officer in the U.S. Army after completing ROTC and served for over three years.
He applied repeatedly to the FBI and was eventually accepted after persistent effort despite initial lack of response.
Rogers drove across the country in four days to attend the FBI Academy after being notified of an opening.
Rogers believes bipartisanship is possible but requires intentional effort and willingness to face criticism.
The rise of social media has increased polarization and reduced opportunities for civil discourse among political figures.
Gerald Ford observed that the shift from driving to Washington via U-Haul to flying back home eroded personal connections among lawmakers.
Marty Peterson was the first female CIA officer to run a senior agent in Moscow and endured significant risks during her assignment.
